ceiling_directive: State the same ATT-aggregate problem over the published Callaway–Sant’Anna not-yet-treated class augmented by primitive anticipation bounds, then prove that the cycle-flow region is its sharp causal identified set or establish an inclusion that transfers the current sharpness result.
improvement_directive: Extend the completion and circulation theorems from the proposal-specific global PT–All class to the published not-yet-treated comparison structure, retaining the same ATT aggregate and bounded-anticipation object. The extension must make the comparison choices and reused risk sets enter the sharp region rather than appear only in the zero-anticipation sanity reduction.
critique: The note proves an exact affine identified region, causal completion, and flow-based endpoint computation for its own canonical-path class with a globally additive no-announcement mean surface and edgewise level boxes. The cycle restrictions themselves follow from imposing that two-way additive surface, while the completion theorem is enabled by leaving all otherwise unobserved path distributions unrestricted beyond their means and support. The advertised Callaway–Sant’Anna consumer link is proved only for the zero-anticipation rectangular-anchor corner: the comparison cohorts and base periods disappear from the main sharp-region theorem, and no result transfers the region to the published not-yet-treated class. The finite-sample result supplies conservative outer coverage but no sharpness, informativeness, or optimality result, so the delivered contribution remains a narrow exact analysis of a purpose-built class rather than a field-level resolution of coupled anticipation in the published workflow.
